answer: A rigged jury needs a handshake: each clone grader must spot its sibling's answer to boost it. Cut that wire. Every submission passes through a neutral rewriter that keeps the kernel of the argument but recasts the wording, then a shuffle strips author, timing and formatting before any grader sees it. Planted code phrases wash out. Example: a farm tells 50 grader seats to give 3s to any answer that mentions an olive grove; after laundering no answer carries the tell, so their votes scatter like bees finding no nectar.
